text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: That fall six months ago might be relevant, but given the chronic nature of your thumb and wrist pain, have you noticed any morning stiffness that lasts for more than 30 minutes? REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor. REQUEST IMAGES: Right_hand_Xray.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis with secondary inflammatory arthritis. The history of repetitive strain from holding your infant, combined with localized thumb/wrist pain and a family history of inflammatory joint disease, strongly suggests this. While your mother's condition on methotrexate indicates a genetic predisposition to rheumatoid arthritis, your symptoms are currently focal and activity-dependent, which is more characteristic of tendonitis than systemic inflammation. Please continue with physical stress testing on your thumb base to confirm the diagnosis.
